newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil dips with premiums and futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil dips with premiums and futures.

text.p: NWE heating oil fell by up to $5 a tonne on Thursday as weaker premiums combined with sharply lower IPE futures. Diesel premiums were steady to a touch firmer.
March IPE gas oil closed $4.50 weaker at $180.25 a tonnes having traded in a well defined range for much of the day.

Barges were done at March IPE +$4 for Rotterdam refinery material, up to $3 off yesterday's levels. Interest remains muted given mild temperatures across much of the continent and the perception of good supplies given 558,500 tonne physical delivery set against the Feb expiry.
German heating oil was able to attract a strong premium because of increased interest and at least two cargoes were heard done at March IPE +$8.50 and +$8.25 cif Germany.
FOD was not so actively sought and premiums fell nearly $2 to around March IPE +$4.50. There was some talk of premiums as low as +$1-2
"Some people may be talking that low, but I don't think its representative," said one trader.
Diesel premiums gained with a trade concluded for a 20,000 tonne cargo at March IPE +$21.75 cif Le Havre on Feb 25-27 dates compared with talk on Wednesday of +$18.
